primary_claim: Reflective-dialogue QLoRA conditioning of Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct improved the model's consistency-under-pressure score over an unconditioned base model, though less than identity-persona conditioning.

effect.value: Reflective-Dialog: 1.63/1.97/0.93 vs Base: 1.23/0.94/1.10 vs Identity baseline: 1.89/3.40/2.20

stated_future_work: applying reflective dialogs to other possible behaviours and risks
testing with larger models in a more pristine research setting
combining it with pre-training or SFT rather than just light post-training conditioning
limitations_stated: only demonstrated with low compute on a single Colab GPU
tested on one small model (Phi-3-mini) and one target behaviour
the interpretation that reflective-dialogues activated a pre-existing behavioural tendency was the author's hypothesis going in and deserves further scrutiny with more controlled experiments
quote: The reflective-dialogue variant showed a meaningful gain on the targeted behaviour (consistency under paraphrase/reframe pressure), despite no explicit rules, persona scripts, or incentives.
